When, in the calendar people use.

Cause

What made it happen.

Consequence

What changed afterwards, and who paid for it.

Who remembers

Which characters know it, and how they tell it.

modules.label: Relationships
modules.description: Who knows whom, how they feel, and what goes unsaid.

pages.title: Relationship web
pages.html:
Who and to whom

Two people, and how they are connected.

Type

Family, ally, rival, lover, employer, or something harder to name.

History

What happened between them that still counts.

Tension

What they want from each other that they cannot say.

Change

How the relationship shifts over the story.

pages.title: Relationship template
pages.html:
First meeting

Where they met, and what each made of the other.

What each wants

The need behind the way they treat each other.

Trust

What it would take to earn it, and what would break it.

Conflict

What they fight about, and what the fight is really about.

Turning point

The scene where the relationship changes direction.

modules.label: Encyclopedia
modules.description: Lore entries and a glossary of invented terms.

pages.title: Lore entry
pages.html:
Term

The name readers will meet.

Definition

What it means in one sentence.

Origin

Where the word or idea came from.

First mention

Where the story explains it, and how much is assumed.

Related entries

What else to read alongside this.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.html:
Terms

Every invented word that needs a definition.

Spelling

How each term is spelled, and the variants to avoid.

Capitalisation

Which words are names, and which are common nouns.

In-world source

Who in the world would define it this way.

Reader confusion

Terms too close to each other, and how to tell them apart.

modules.label: Plot & structure
modules.description: Premise, act structure, subplots, and open threads.

pages.title: Premise
pages.html:
One line

The story in a sentence, without names.

Situation

What is wrong with the world when the story opens.

Protagonist wants

What they pursue, and why now.

Obstacle

What stands in the way, and why it cannot be avoided.

Stakes

What is lost if they fail.

pages.title: Act structure
pages.html:
Act one

The setup, the inciting event, and the door closing behind them.

Act two

Escalations, reversals, and the point of no return.

Midpoint

The discovery that changes what the story is about.

Act three

The confrontation, and what it costs.

Ending

What the last page leaves the reader with.

pages.title: Subplots and threads
pages.html:
Subplots

Each secondary story, and how it touches the main one.

Open threads

Questions raised and still waiting for an answer.

Callbacks

Details planted early that pay off late.

Foreshadowing

What the reader should suspect before the character does.

Cut

Ideas you dropped, and where they went.

modules.description: Sources, facts, and the things you still have to check.

pages.title: Sources
pages.html:
Books

Secondary works, with author and year.

Articles and archives

Documents, registers, letters, and where to find them.

People to ask

Experts, locals, and the questions worth putting to them.

Sites and objects

Places to visit, and museum pieces worth seeing.

Reliability

Where sources disagree, and which you trust.

pages.title: Facts to verify
pages.html:
Claim

The fact the story depends on.

Where found

Where you found it, with page or link.

Confidence

How sure you are, and what would raise it.

Where it appears

The scene or chapter that uses it.

Check by

When to settle it, and who can help.
